description: Working together to turn NASA Earth science data into meaningful environmental insights.
summary:
EarthTrend is an interactive Earth science analysis platform developed for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026, addressing the challenge “Be An Earth System Trend Detective!”. It enables users to explore environmental changes over time by selecting variables, locations, data sources, and date ranges. Using NASA Earth observation and model-based datasets, EarthTrend transforms complex scientific data into interactive visualizations and statistical analyses that reveal the direction and rate of environmental trends.

The platform combines trend estimation methods with statistical significance testing, while accounting for seasonality, temporal dependence, and data limitations. It also provides beginner-friendly explanations and evidence-based insights to help users understand what the results mean and what further investigation may be useful.

By making Earth science data more accessible and interpretable, EarthTrend helps users investigate where environmental conditions are changing, how much they are changing, and whether the available evidence supports a statistically significant trend.
details:
How EarthTrend Works

EarthTrend is an interactive platform that helps users investigate changes in Earth's environmental systems over time. Users can select an environmental variable, a geographic location or region, a data source, and a time range. The platform retrieves or processes the corresponding datasets and presents the results through interactive charts and statistical summaries.

EarthTrend analyzes the data using methods such as Ordinary Least Squares (OLS) regression with seasonal fixed effects, Sen's slope, and the Mann–Kendall trend test. It also considers seasonality, temporal autocorrelation, missing observations, and data coverage when determining whether statistical inference can be performed. When the available data are insufficient, the platform clearly explains the limitation instead of presenting unsupported conclusions.

Benefits and Intended Impact

Earth science datasets can be complex and difficult for non-specialists to interpret. EarthTrend makes these datasets more accessible by translating statistical outputs into understandable explanations and evidence-based insights. Users can explore whether an environmental variable is increasing or decreasing, estimate the rate of change, assess statistical significance when appropriate, and identify where further investigation may be needed.

The intended impact is to support environmental awareness, data literacy, and informed exploration of Earth system trends. The platform is designed as an educational and analytical tool, not as a forecasting or causal-detection system.

Tools and Technologies

EarthTrend was developed using Python and Streamlit. Its main technologies and libraries include:

  • Streamlit: Interactive web application interface.
  • Pandas and NumPy: Data processing, organization, and numerical calculations.
  • SciPy and Statsmodels: Scientific and statistical analysis.
  • PyMannKendall: Mann–Kendall trend analysis.
  • Plotly: Interactive data visualizations.
  • Requests: Communication with data APIs.
  • Pytest: Automated testing and quality assurance.

The project uses NASA data services, including NASA POWER and NASA Giovanni, to access Earth science datasets. No specialized hardware is required; the application runs as a software-based platform.

Creativity and Design Considerations

EarthTrend combines data exploration, statistical safeguards, interactive visualization, and beginner-friendly interpretation in one platform. Rather than simply displaying a trend line, it distinguishes between an observed trend and a statistically supported conclusion.

During development, the team considered data reliability, spatial and temporal coverage, seasonal patterns, missing values, temporal dependence, differences between data sources, and the risk of misleading interpretations. These considerations help users understand not only what the data show, but also the limitations of the available evidence.
